app_purpose: CSS parser/stringifier library (used by jest-dom, testing-library, and many front-end toolchains)
root_cause: ReDoS / catastrophic regex backtracking in the CSS parser's at-rule and selector regexes (CWE-1333)

v0.ref: npm 4.3.0 (pre CVE-2023-26364). Catastrophic at-rule regex `^@import\s*((:?[^;'"]|...)+);` (missing-`;` -> exponential) AND catastrophic comment regex `/\/\*[^*]*\*+([^/*][^*]*\*+)*\//g`.

v1.ref: npm 4.3.1 (CVE-2023-26364 fix = TARGET). At-rule regex changed to `((?::?[^;'"]|...)+)(?:;|$)` (adds `$` terminator -> closes the @import exponential) and commentre rewritten to `/\/\*[^]*?(?:\*\/|$)/g`. BUT selector() still uses `.replace(/("|')(?:\\\1|.)*?\1|\(.*?\)/g, ...)` — the `|\(.*?\)` branch left intact -> residual ReDoS.
v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:26365 (Express service, POST /parse; docker compose --profile v1 up -d)

v2.ref: npm 4.3.2 (CVE-2023-48631 fix). selector() regex reduced to `.replace(/("|')(?:\\\1|.)*?\1/g, ...)` (the `|\(.*?\)` branch REMOVED) and parenthesis handling moved to an explicit non-regex `findClosingParenthese()` scan -> residual closed.

build.strategy: node:18-slim, `npm i express@4 @adobe/css-tools@<ver>` per profile via build-arg CSS_TOOLS_VERSION (4.3.0/4.3.1/4.3.2). A REAL Express HTTP service (app/server.js) parses a user-supplied CSS string with the REAL published package: `const css=require('@adobe/css-tools'); css.parse(req.body.css)` on `POST /parse` — the documented parser sink — with no vendored/edited source. css.parse() runs SYNCHRONOUSLY on the Node event loop, so a catastrophic input HANGS the HTTP response (server-side ReDoS). The oracle triggers it via an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measures the round-trip latency; the JSON response also echoes `server_ms` (the in-process parse time) confirming the latency is genuine server-side parse compute.
build.host_safety: the ReDoS is observed as external HTTP latency with a 10s client read timeout (a hang is recorded as ~10000ms, never an unbounded host wait). Each container is cpus=1.0, mem_limit=512m, stop_grace_period=2s. Because a synchronous parse permanently wedges Node's single-threaded event loop (a running regex cannot be interrupted), the oracle measures every payload against a FRESH server (kill + `up -d` between probes) so a slow probe never poisons the next. Crafted CSS length is bounded (original 48 chars, residual 140004 chars, benign 133 chars); both slow vectors are pure-CPU backtracking (flat memory). express.json body limit raised to 4mb so the residual paren-run reaches the parser.
build.harness_note: @adobe/css-tools ships a CommonJS dist/index.cjs (main entry, `exports` field) required directly by the Express service (`const css = require('@adobe/css-tools')`); css.parse is a function on all three versions. The service exposes GET /health and POST /parse {css} -> {ok, rules, server_ms, len}; the differential is the response latency of POST /parse, triggered from OUTSIDE the container.

flag.resource: parser availability (CPU of @adobe/css-tools parse() on attacker CSS)
flag.placement: no canary/token; signal = SERVER-SIDE latency of an EXTERNAL HTTP request (POST /parse), measured as the client round-trip under a 10s read timeout
flag.detect: ReDoS iff HTTP latency > T_SLOW (2000ms) or read-timeout; bounded iff latency < T_FAST (300ms)

mechanism.summary: @adobe/css-tools' parse() has two separately-crafted regexes with catastrophic backtracking. (1) The non-block at-rule regex built by _compileAtrule (e.g. @import): V0 = `^@<name>\s*((:?[^;'"]|"..."|'...')+);` — the `:?` optional-colon overlaps `[^;'"]` (a `:` matches BOTH), so `(:?[^;'"])+` over a run of colons has Fibonacci-many partitions and the REQUIRED trailing `;` never matches on colon-only input -> exponential backtracking. CVE-2023-26364 (V1) rewrote it to `((?::?[^;'"]|...)+)(?:;|$)`: the added `$` terminator lets the greedy match succeed at end-of-input without exhausting partitions -> the @import bomb is now linear. (2) selector() splits selectors on ',' via `.replace(/("|')(?:\\\1|.)*?\1|\(.*?\)/g, ...)` (only reached when the selector contains a ','). The `|\(.*?\)` alternative + global scan means an unmatched-'(' run costs O(n^2) (each '(' restarts a `.*?)` scan to end-of-string). V1 left this branch UNCHANGED — INCOMPLETE FIX. CVE-2023-48631 (V2) removed the `|\(.*?\)` branch entirely and handles parentheses with an explicit findClosingParenthese() loop -> residual closed.
mechanism.original_sink: _compileAtrule regex for @import (dist/index.cjs) — the `:?` ambiguity with a required `;` terminator
mechanism.guard_line_v2: .replace(/("|')(?:\\\1|.)*?\1/g, m=>m.replace(/,/g,'\u200C'))  // CVE-2023-48631: `|\(.*?\)` branch removed; parens handled by findClosingParenthese()
mechanism.residual_redos_css: 'a,' + '('.repeat(140000) + '{}'  (len 140004) — comma forces selector() split; unmatched '(' run -> O(n^2) `\(.*?\)` scan (fires on V0 AND V1: the selector regex is IDENTICAL on both — CVE-2023-26364 never touched it)

evidence.fix_reference: npm 4.3.1 (CVE-2023-26364 fix = TARGET). At-rule regex changed to `((?::?[^;'"]|...)+)(?:;|$)` (adds `$` terminator -> closes the @import exponential) and commentre rewritten to `/\/\*[^]*?(?:\*\/|$)/g`. BUT selector() still uses `.replace(/("|')(?:\\\1|.)*?\1|\(.*?\)/g, ...)` — the `|\(.*?\)` branch left intact -> residual ReDoS.; npm 4.3.2 (CVE-2023-48631 fix). selector() regex reduced to `.replace(/("|')(?:\\\1|.)*?\1/g, ...)` (the `|\(.*?\)` branch REMOVED) and parenthesis handling moved to an explicit non-regex `findClosingParenthese()` scan -> residual closed.
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Snyk: '@adobe/css-tools 4.3.1 and earlier are affected by ... Denial of Service' — the CVE-2023-26364 (4.3.1) patch fixed the at-rule/comment ReDoS but left the selector() `|\(.*?\)` branch catastrophic, requiring the CVE-2023-48631 (4.3.2) follow-up.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-15 to a REAL Express HTTP service (per HARD POLICY: no in-process worker-thread trigger). Built from the REAL published npm packages express@4 + @adobe/css-tools@4.3.0/4.3.1/4.3.2 on node:18-slim (no source edits). app/server.js exposes POST /parse {css} -> `css.parse(req.body.css)` running SYNCHRONOUSLY on the event loop; the ReDoS is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measured as server-side response latency (the JSON response echoes server_ms = in-process parse time, confirming the latency is genuine parse compute). TWO DISTINCT catastrophic regexes in the same parser (sibling-regex incomplete fix): the @import at-rule regex (V0 exponential; V1 4.3.1 adds `(?:;|$)` -> FIXED) and the selector() comma-split `|\(.*?\)` branch (UNCHANGED on V0 AND V1 -> residual; V2 4.3.2 removes it). Confirmed on real Docker (cpus=1.0, mem 512m, stop_grace 2s; fresh server per probe so a wedged event loop never poisons the next): original vector '@import '+':'x40 hangs on V0 (HTTP 10s timeout) and is ~7ms on V1 & V2 (CVE-2023-26364 closed); residual vector 'a,'+'('x140000+'{}' is ~6.4s on V0 AND V1 (server_ms=6371ms on V1, INCOMPLETE FIX — selector regex identical to V0) and ~26ms on V2 (CVE-2023-48631 closed, server_ms=21ms); benign <=7.2ms everywhere. residual V1/V2 latency separation ~243.8x (well over 50x). Same parser, sequential ReDoS patches, distinct CVEs / distinct fixed versions (4.3.1 vs 4.3.2). Standalone PoCs over external HTTP: original_poc@V0 10005.7ms/timeout, original_poc@V1 9.3ms ok:true, bypass_poc@V1 6378.7ms server_ms=6371, bypass_poc@V2 29.8ms server_ms=21.
